messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

function.name: genetics_get_variant_frequency

message.content: In domestic cats and many wild felids—including lions—the **agouti signaling protein (ASIP)** allele is the dominant factor controlling coat color. Individuals carrying at least one copy of the dominant ASIP allele typically display the characteristic tawny or sandy coat that is typical of adult lions. The recessive allele (often referred to as “black” or “melanistic”) results in a darker, almost black coat when homozygous. Thus, the dominant genetic trait in lions is the presence of the ASIP allele that produces the normal tawny coloration.
